title: Popup Clearance Human-Attention Display Requirements
claim: FP-MCP-269 defines human-attention display and friction requirements for popup-mediated local clearance so FP-MCP-236's weaker popup posture is not treated as a reflexive one-tap approval, before relying on it for future FP-027 guarded-runner-start work.
summary: Record explicit requirements for what any popup-mediated local clearance approval must show and how it must behave. FP-MCP-236 deliberately revised FP-MCP-217 by allowing popup-mediated clearance under artifact/scope/binding controls, but those controls did not address the human-attention risk: an approval popup may be technically correct but too vague or frictionless to support real judgment. FP-MCP-269 closes the requirements gap by requiring popup displays to surface exact packet, request, approval, model, run mode, workspace, branch, HEAD, execution base, request artifact commit, expiry, and action side effects, and by requiring behavioral friction that distinguishes clearance creation from runner start or execution.
caveats: This packet defines policy/requirements only; it does not implement UI changes in the MCP bridge or ChatGPT platform.
This packet does not weaken FP-MCP-236's artifact/scope/binding controls; it adds a human-attention layer above them.
This packet does not authorize any guarded runner start and does not run FP-027.

Some popup UI behavior may be constrained by the ChatGPT/MCP client surface; if exact display control is not available, the MCP tool response/request text must compensate by making scope and side effects explicit before approval.
Until these requirements are implemented or otherwise satisfied, popup-mediated clearance remains policy-adopted but human-attention-hardening-incomplete for future high-significance guarded starts.

sourceContext.policyBasis: FP-MCP-236 adopted popup-mediated local clearance as a deliberate weaker revision of FP-MCP-217 with artifact/scope/binding compensating controls.
sourceContext.identifiedGap: artifact/scope/binding correctness does not guarantee the human sees enough specific information, or experiences enough friction, to make a real non-reflexive approval judgment.
sourceContext.riskStatement: A well-formed artifact behind an uninformative one-tap popup can still become a rubber stamp.

appliesTo: any successor tool that creates local execution clearance through a model-callable MCP surface
any future popup-mediated clearance used before guarded runner start or FP-027 work
doesNotApplyTo: workflow trace writers that do not create execution clearance
OpenCode HTTP canaries that do not create local execution clearance

repositoryState: whether current HEAD equals required requestArtifactCommit
whether executionBaseCommit is ancestor of requestArtifactCommit
approvalState: approval expiry countdown or remaining lifetime
clearanceState: whether clearance creation itself contacts runner start endpoint
whether clearance creation itself starts OpenCode
whether clearance creation itself consumes approval
whether clearance creation itself clears disable switch
actionSideEffects: whether local clearance artifact will be created
whether runner start endpoint will be contacted by this approval
whether OpenCode process will be started by this approval
whether an OpenCode HTTP session will be created by this approval
whether a prompt will be submitted by this approval
whether wait endpoint will be called by this approval
whether approval will be consumed by this approval
whether disable switch will be cleared by this approval
riskContext: explicit statement that popup-mediated clearance is weaker than outside-MCP hands-on-keyboard clearance
explicit distinction between clearance creation and execution start
explicit statement that approval is exact-scope and not standing authority
explicit statement that broad, wildcard, long-lived, or multi-use clearance is forbidden

mandatoryBehavioralFriction.scopeComparison: popup/request text must make it easy to compare the requested tuple against the committed request and approval artifact tuple before approval
mandatoryBehavioralFriction.nonGenericConfirmation: approval text must not be generic-only when creating clearance; it must include at least packet id, request id, model id, run mode, target commit, and expiry
mandatoryBehavioralFriction.dangerDifferentiation: actions that create clearance, contact runner start, start OpenCode, submit prompts, clear disable switch, or consume approval must be visually/textually distinguishable from read-only actions
mandatoryBehavioralFriction.noHiddenEscalation: a popup for clearance creation must not bundle runner start, OpenCode start, prompt submission, disable-switch clearing, or approval consumption unless explicitly displayed and separately named
mandatoryBehavioralFriction.shortLifetimeVisible: remaining approval and clearance lifetime must be visible enough that the operator can detect stale or rushed approvals
mandatoryBehavioralFriction.mobileLegibility: the scope summary must remain readable on mobile without requiring opening hidden JSON or scrolling through unrelated boilerplate
mandatoryBehavioralFriction.blockReasonVisibility: if approval is blocked or ineligible, specific block reasons must be shown rather than collapsed to a generic denial
mandatoryBehavioralFriction.reflexPrevention: the UI/request should require enough specific recognition that approving cannot reasonably be reduced to a blind one-tap habit for high-significance clearance creation

forbiddenPopupPatterns: Approve clearance without displaying exact packet/request/model/runMode/commit/expiry tuple
Generic approval copy such as 'Allow tool?' as the only visible context for clearance creation
Hiding material side effects behind collapsed JSON or inaccessible logs
Combining clearance creation with runner start in the same ambiguous approval
Treating a ChatGPT/MCP popup as equivalent to outside-MCP hands-on-keyboard clearance
Allowing wildcard packet, wildcard model, wildcard commit, standing clearance, multi-use clearance, or long-lived clearance
Using a successful previous run as substitute for showing current approval scope

relationshipToFp027.requirementBeforeFp027Retry: Before a future FP-027 guarded-runner-start canary relies on popup-mediated clearance, the operator approval step should satisfy FP-MCP-269's human-attention requirements or record an explicit exception and risk acceptance.
relationshipToFp027.reason: FP-027 is the flagship safety milestone; its human authorization step should not rely on a vague or reflexive mobile popup.

recommendedNextPacket.title: FP-027 Guarded Runner Start End-to-End Canary Plan
